newsitem.title: UK: Top BoE officals had little notice of reform.
newsitem.headline: Top BoE officals had little notice of reform.

text.p: Senior officials at the Bank of England (BOE), including BoE Governor Eddie George, had little advance knowledge of Tuesday's major reforms to the central bank's status, sources familiar with the situation told Reuters.
One person close to the Bank said the Labour Government only put the proposals to George on Monday.

On Tuesday, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown unveiled plans to form a monetary policy committee and give the BOE "operational responsibility" for interest rate policy in order to meet government inflation objectives.
The moves are among the most far-reaching in the Bank's history, which spans more than 300 years.
Asked what kind of notice the Bank had of Brown's intentions, one source said, "Not a lot," although the surprise was characterised as a pleasant one.
Another source said the moves were not known among many Bank staff in advance.
